title: Booleans

items.title: The Boolean Type: True and False
items.content:
A **boolean** (`bool`) represents one of only two possible truth values:
- `True`
- `False`

In Python, both literals **must be capitalized**. Writing lowercase `true` or `false` causes a `NameError` because Python thinks you are referring to an undefined variable.
items.explanation: Booleans represent binary truth states. They must always begin with an uppercase letter: True or False.

items.prompt: Why is `x = 5` valid while `5 = x` is a `SyntaxError` in Python?
options: = assigns the right-hand value to the variable name on the left; a number literal cannot be assigned into
Variables can only be defined in even numbered lines
Python requires numbers to come after strings
items.correct_answer: = assigns the right-hand value to the variable name on the left; a number literal cannot be assigned into
items.explanation: The target of an assignment must be an identifier (variable), never an immutable literal like 5.
items.mental_model: A single equals sign (=) is a command: "make this name point to this value". A double equals sign (==) is a question: "do these two values match?"
